title_en: Bloomberg’s Eric Balchunas on the Index Fund That Changed Investing
title_zh: Bloomberg 的 Eric Balchunas 谈改变投资行业的指数基金
subtitle_zh: Vanguard 500 指数基金 50 周年回望 Bogle 效应，并盘点 USBG、FRUT 等新 ETF 发行潮。
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Prime 由 Nate Geraci 主持，同样是双段结构：开篇与 VettaFi 资深行业分析师 Kirsten Chang 盘点近期铺天盖地的新 ETF 发行，随后连线 Bloomberg 资深 ETF 分析师 Eric Balchunas，回望改变投资行业的指数基金。Chang 指出今年新发行已突破一千只、仅八月就约一百五十只，比去年同期创纪录节奏快约五成，其中约八成是主动产品；发行商正竞相为顾问提供手术刀级精度的工具箱，涵盖结果型结构、期权收益叠加、主动信用与 AI 细分基础设施。Geraci 补充今年已有十七只新 ETF 资产破亿，只要做中一只便足以支撑发行商持续涌入。重头戏是 Balchunas 解读 Vanguard 第一只指数投资信托诞生五十周年、以及由它演变而来、资产超一万亿美元的 VOO。作为 The Bogle Effect 一书作者、曾与 Jack Bogle 本人对谈的他认为，这只基金之所以成为史上最具影响力的基金，根源在于 Bogle 把 Vanguard 建成一家由持有人共同所有（mutual ownership）的后台公司——这一结构才是过去五十年乃至百年的秘密武器，几乎每一个行业趋势顺着线头往上捋都会回到一九七四年 Bogle 的构想。他还谈到 Vanguard 不付渠道分销费、二零零八年金融危机中主动管理失灵如何共同助推指数化与费用聚焦，并以 BlackRock、Fidelity 为对照剖析谁能真正与共同所有制结构竞争。是一集把指数基金思想史与当下发行潮并置的深度回望。

turns.en: But a three basis point index fund is, you know, investor utopia, there's a world of difference there. And the only reason it's three is because the Vanguard mutual ownership structure. So therefore, I think indexing would be around but, you know, a sliver of where it is on the flip side, let's say indexing the concept never was born and it was only active and Vanguard was born a back office manager and they started
turns.zh: 但一个 3 个基点的指数基金，那是投资者的乌托邦，两者差着十万八千里。而它能到 3 个基点，唯一的理由就是 Vanguard 的共同所有制结构。所以我认为，指数化会有，但只是现在规模的九牛一毛。反过来讲，如果指数化这个概念压根没诞生，市场只有主动，Vanguard 生而是一家后台管理公司，然后陆续

turns.en: launching active funds down the line. They would have used that mutual ownership structure to lower the fees on the active funds. And I believe they would be the biggest active manager seven or eight times over. Because over the years, their cheaper fees would allow them to bring a gun to a knife fight.
turns.zh: 发行主动基金，他们一定会用共同所有制结构来压低主动基金的费率。我相信他们会成为最大的主动管理人，规模超别人七八倍。因为这么多年下来，更低的费率就等于让他们带着枪上冷兵器战场。

turns.en: And over the 20 year timeframe, all the Vanguard active funds would just beat everybody else instead to be the top of the list. And when they had the stories out on the best managers, Vanguard would dominate simply because of low fees. And that's why I think all the active money would have gone to Vanguard, they would have been the biggest active manager. So Vanguard was going to win based on that mutual ownership structure one way
turns.zh: 把时间拉长到 20 年，Vanguard 旗下所有主动基金就会靠着费用把其他所有人打趴下，霸榜所有榜单。当媒体做“最佳管理人”报道时，Vanguard 会仅凭低费率就占满名单。所以我认为主动的钱都会流向 Vanguard，他们会成为最大的主动管理人。也就是说，凭着共同所有制结构，Vanguard 无论如何都会赢，

turns.en: or another. I just think indexing was the perfect match for it at that particular time. And to be fair to circumstance, Bogle wasn't really allowed to launch any other active funds in the deal he had with Wellington. And he thought, well, this isn't not, it was supposed to be he couldn't launch funds at all. But he used this technicality that you wouldn't manage this fund. In fact, they didn't even call them portfolio managers, they
turns.zh: 无非是赢的方式不同。我只是觉得，在特定的时点，指数化是它的天作之合。公平地说，在 Bogle 和 Wellington 达成的协议里，他其实基本不被允许再发行其他主动基金。他本来以为——按约定他压根不能发任何基金。但他钻了一个空子：这只基金是“不主动管理”的。事实上他们连“组合管理人”都不叫，

turns.en: called them, I think, like execution engineers or something like that, who managed the 500 fund, it wasn't like a manager. So they're like, the board kind of like, let him have it, because it wasn't a real fund. So the index fund was almost like a convenience for him, you know, necessity or what was that phrase? Mother in necessity is the mother of invention. And that applied, I think to Vanguard and the index fund at that time.
turns.zh: 他们管做 500 基金的人叫——我想，类似“执行工程师”之类的头衔——那不算一个经理。所以董事会就大概让他过了这一关，因为那不算一只真正的基金。所以指数基金对他几乎是被逼出来的发明——俗话说，需要是发明之母。我想这句话正好适用于当时的 Vanguard 和指数基金。

turns.en: But again, I asked Bogle point blank in one of my interviews with him, what was the more important invention or a contribution? He said, without a doubt, the mutual ownership structure, that comes first. Everything else springs from that, including the index fund and which is now low cost. And again, people forget the Vanguard index for when it came out in 1975, or 76 was 43 basis points. And it didn't get cheap
turns.zh: 但我要再说一遍，我在一次采访里直截了当地问过 Bogle：哪个发明或贡献更重要？他说，毫无疑问，是共同所有制结构。那是第一位的，其他一切——包括指数基金，也就是现在的低成本——都从中生长出来。还有，人们常常忘记：Vanguard 指数基金 1975、76 年问世时收费 43 个基点，一直到

turns.en: until it got to, I don't know, like the 90s. And so if you look at the assets of the Vanguard index fund, it's flat for 20 years, nobody cared. I mean, it was like, it was like 500 million, a billion, two billion, and he took victory laps every year, but it was one billion. Now Voo takes in a billion a day.
turns.zh: 我不确定，大概到 90 年代才真正变便宜。所以你看这只 Vanguard 指数基金的资产，20 年纹丝不动，没人搭理。规模在 5 亿、10 亿、20 亿之间打转，他每年都要为它绕场庆祝，也就 10 亿美元。而现在 VOO 一天就能吸进 10 亿。

turns.en: But anyway, go back to then, it went like this. And then the fee was coming like this. And right around 2008, you had the market crash where managers like failed to sidestep the crash, and that turned people off. You had Vanguard getting down below 10 bath vips, and you had the internet spreading all the information and making everything more readily available. And that is when indexing went parabolic. So to me, around
turns.zh: 不过回到当年，资产大概这样走，费率这样往下压。大约到 2008 年，市场崩盘，主动经理人们没能躲过那场崩盘，把投资者劝退了。Vanguard 的费率降到 10 个基点以下，互联网又在传播一切信息、让一切唾手可得。就在那一刻，指数化开始抛物线式增长。所以在我看来，大约

turns.en: 2008 is when everything came together. But it was really those low fees that kicked in that were really important. So what's funny is 99.8% of all that 22 trillion in index fund assets came after Bogle stepped down as Vanguard CEO. It's remarkable.
turns.zh: 到 2008 年，所有要素才凑齐。但真正重要的，还是那批低费率的落地。有意思的是：那 22 万亿美元的指数基金资产里，99.8% 都是在 Bogle 卸任 Vanguard CEO 之后才积累的。太惊人了。

turns.en: Tell me that's not an insane fun fact. He was only there for 0.2% of all of all of that. And he was there for over 20 years. That's how long it took not to mention they they put the index fund out outside of the system with no distribution fees. So you had to like leave your big wirehouse brokerage to go get it.
turns.zh: 你敢说这不是一个疯狂趣闻？他只占那段历史的 0.2%，而他任职超过 20 年——事情就是花了那么久。更别提他们最初是把指数基金放在体系之外发行的，不付任何渠道分销费用，所以你非得离开大型券商（wirehouse）才能买到它。

turns.en: And you're an RIA. I actually give him credit for launching the RIA movement to a degree or at least exacerbating because if you wanted Vanguard, you had to leave your big mothership firm and set up an independent advisory firm.
turns.zh: 而你就是 RIA。我倒真觉得，他在很大程度上——至少是推波助澜——催生了 RIA 运动，因为你要想买 Vanguard，就得离开那艘大航母公司，自己出去开一家独立顾问公司。

turns.en: You hit on so many great trends there. I agree with all of that because if you look at this, it really is a fee story more than it is an indexing story. Now indexing plays a role here because we know historically how difficult it is for active managers to beat those indexes. But a big part of that is because of the fee. And you have the perfect storm here where the fund launched, you mentioned, you know, spy launching in 1993, then
turns.zh: 你点出了太多重要的脉络了，我全都同意。因为说到底，这更像是一个“费用”的故事，而不只是“指数化”的故事。指数化在这里当然有作用，因为我们知道历史上主动管理人要跑赢那些指数有多难，但那其中很大一部分原因就是费用。于是你看到这个完美风暴：基金发行了——你提到 SPY 是 1993 年发行的，然后

turns.en: you had the proliferation of the internet in the early 2000s. So that allowed investors to much more easily be able to compare performance and cost data. And that started putting a lot more focus on index funds and what their costs, you know, what the costs were. And then the rise of the fee based investment advisor, where you had this shift away from the commission based models and, you know, Vanguard not paying distribution fees to,
turns.zh: 2000 年代初互联网开始普及，投资者能更容易地比较业绩和成本数据，市场的注意力开始更多聚焦在指数基金及其成本上。然后是收费型投资顾问的崛起，行业从佣金模式往那边迁移。而 Vanguard 不付渠道分销费、不靠别人推产品，这也起了作用。然后你还提到 2008 年

turns.en: you know, to have their products pushed that played a role. And then you also mentioned the 2008 global financial crisis where we saw active managers were unable to sidestep that. I think all of this played in clearly to the rise of indexing overall and this focus on fees, going back to the mutual ownership structure, which we both agree, that's the secret sauce here.
turns.zh: 全球金融危机，我们看到主动管理人没能绕开那场灾难。我觉得这一切都助推了指数化的整体崛起和这场对费用的聚焦。回到共同所有制结构——我们俩都同意——那才是这里的秘密武器。

turns.en: Do you think anybody can ever compete with that? Like obviously Vanguard has plenty of competitors, some of whom even offer lower cost funds in certain categories. But this mutual ownership structure just feels like such an embedded advantage, where these other firms probably have to work twice as hard to compete. And so like, will anybody ever, you know, try a mutual ownership structure like Vanguard? Or how do you think
turns.zh: 你觉得有人能真正与之竞争吗？显然 Vanguard 有很多对手，某些类别里甚至有人提供更便宜的产品。但共同所有制结构感觉是一种刻在骨子里的优势，其他公司可能得付出加倍的努力才能竞争。那么，会有人尝试搞 Vanguard 式的共同所有制吗？还是说你觉得

turns.en: that the competition plays out longer term? You know, even Bogle was surprised nobody tried it since then. And, you know, this is why I was so fascinated by Bogle the man and why I named the book the Bogle effect, because no person goes to Wall Street to like give over all the profits to the investors, it just doesn't make economic sense. And it's an anomaly in physics. It's just a odd thing that you almost
turns.zh: 长期的竞争会怎么演化？你知道，连 Bogle 自己都惊讶后来居然没人效仿。这也是为什么我对 Bogle 这个人如此着迷，为什么我把书名叫 The Bogle Effect——因为没人跑到华尔街是为了把利润全数交给投资者的，这在经济上说不通。它几乎是物理学意义上的异类，是一件你几乎不能

turns.en: have to like, not study through your normal lens. He was weird. And there was a situation with Wellington that helped the situation. But Bogle was also I think just designed different that's why chapter four, my book is called explaining Bogle.
turns.zh: 用常规视角去研究的事。他很怪。Wellington 那边的特殊情况也促成了这件事。但我认为 Bogle 天生就构造不同——所以我书的第四章就叫 Explaining Bogle。

turns.en: Because you almost have to go what went into this brain to make him do such a crazy thing that you haven't seen since. And he was just, it was circumstance, there's also how he was raised.
turns.zh: 因为你几乎得去探究：这颗大脑里到底装了什么，才让他做出那种此后没人再做过的大胆事。那有境遇的因素，也有他成长背景的塑造。

turns.en: Anyway, long story short, I don't think you'll find anybody copying it. But here's the thing, there's no need anymore. That mutual ownership structure is the governing force of everything now. Like, you're already under its spell. It owns you because we have a note coming out tomorrow. And I'll go ahead and front myself a little bit because but I've already talked about this. Vanguard's market share has grown for 50
turns.zh: 不管怎么说，长话短说：我认为你不会看到有人复制它。但有意思的是，现在已经不需要了。共同所有制结构已经是如今一切的主宰力量——你已经在它的影响之下，某种意义上它“拥有”你。明天我们会发一篇报告，我先给自己剧透一下，之前我也聊过这事：Vanguard 的市场份额增长了 50 年，

turns.en: years, but it just started to decline. It hit a peak at 27%, meaning it had 27% of all the fund assets that's mutual fund plus ETFs. That's a high watermark. The last high watermark was Fidelity at 14% in the 90s. And so we were watching this number because it's like, when will Vanguard finally like get plateau and it has plateaued and it's even come down a tad. Why?
turns.zh: 但最近开始下滑了。它在 27% 见顶——也就是说它占了全部基金资产——共同基金加 ETF——的 27%，这是历史高点。上一个高水是 90 年代 Fidelity 的 14%。我们一直在盯这个数字，心想 Vanguard 什么时候终于会 plateau，现在它真的见顶了，甚至还回落了一点点。为什么？

turns.en: Two big reasons are Fidelity and BlackRock both have very low cost ETFs and index mutual funds. Fidelity is 500 Vanguard in you know, type. Well, I'll just rephrase that. Fidelity is 500 index fund, which is that, you know, basically a Vanguard rip off has 800 and like $50 billion. People don't know about it because it's a mutual fund. And you know, we don't cover mutual funds anymore, but it is a stud. It's four times over
turns.zh: 两大原因：Fidelity 和 BlackRock 都有非常低成本的 ETF 和指数共同基金。Fidelity 有 500——我换个说法——Fidelity 500 指数共同基金，基本就是照抄 Vanguard 的那只，规模大概 500 亿美元。大家不知道它，因为它是一只共同基金。你知道，我们现在不太覆盖共同基金了，但它真的是头猛兽——它现在是

turns.en: their biggest mutual fund now. It charges one basis point. So they're actually cheaper than Vanguard. And I can't imagine they love that it's that popular, but I give them credit for at least doing it because it it helped turn around their flows.
turns.zh: Fidelity 最大的共同基金，是原来最大一只的四倍。它只收 1 个基点，实际上比 Vanguard 还便宜。我不敢想象他们有多“喜欢”它这么火，但至少我给他们点个赞：他们做了，而且它扭转了他们的净流量。

turns.en: And it offset some of the active outflows. So you have Fidelity gaining market share. And you have BlackRock gaining market share because of IVV, but also BlackRock does so many things that you don't realize they to me BlackRock's real strategy is hustle points. They just do they run every trend down, whether it's ESG or themes or crypto, they are not lazy. And so they've been able to actually increase their market share. Then you
turns.zh: 也抵消了一些主动产品的净流出。于是 Fidelity 在扩大市场份额；BlackRock 也在扩大市场份额，靠的是 IVV，但不仅如此——BlackRock 做的很多事你没意识到。对我来说，BlackRock 真正的战略就是拼“努力值”：每一个趋势他们都跑到底，不管是 ESG、主题还是加密，他们绝不偷懒。所以他们确实提高了市场份额。然后再把

turns.en: throw in JP Morgan has B bus, which is very much like Vanguard, then you have Goldman has Jesus, which is like Vanguard, in Vesco, State Street spy M is now two basis points, it's going to be in Trump accounts. Wherever you look, all the big guys, especially especially the top 10, they all basically had to copy Vanguard and it worked. They're they're now seeing inflows. And this to me is the absolute realization of Bogle's
turns.zh: JPMorgan 的 B bus 算进去，它非常像 Vanguard；Goldman 的 Jesus 也是学 Vanguard 的；Invesco、State Street——SPY 现在只有 2 个基点，而且会被纳入 Trump 账户（Trump Accounts）。你看遍每个角落，所有大厂——尤其是前十名——实际上都在抄 Vanguard，而且抄成了，他们现在都有净流入。而在我看来，这正是 Bogle 梦想的

turns.en: dream. When I was researching the book on him, I was shocked at this thing. I read some of his quotes back in the day. But I don't remember this one. And it was something to the effect of, I told these Harvard Business School students that I'll know that Vanguard's mission is beginning to be accomplished when our market share begins to erode. And so we kept writing his notes saying Vanguard's killing it, but Bogle's dream is
turns.zh: 彻底实现。我当年为他写书做研究时，被一段话震住了。他的一些老引言我读过，但这一句我不记得了。大意是：我跟这些哈佛商学院的学生说过，什么时候我看到我们的市场份额开始被侵蚀，那就是 Vanguard 的使命开始完成的时候。所以媒体一直在写 Vanguard 一骑绝尘，但 Bogle 的梦想

turns.en: still elusive. And so I was waiting for the day when Bogle's dream will come true. And ironically, it happened right around 50 years. So in this 50 year cycle, it took that long. And he said, because that will mean everybody else is giving people a good deal. If our market share erodes. And so this is a massive grand vision that you have here of a whole industry, not just the firm. And the idea that he would say that in 91, this was back
turns.zh: 始终还差一步。我一直在等 Bogle 梦想成真那一天。讽刺的是，它恰好发生在 50 年整——这个 50 年周期，它就是这么久。他的逻辑是：如果我们的市场份额被侵蚀，那就说明其他人也在给投资者好交易。这是对整个行业——而不只一家公司——的宏大愿景。而且他 1991 年就说出这种话，那时候

turns.en: again, when indexing had 0.2% of the assets it has now, Vanguard's market share was tiny. And to have that vision to see all this play out, and to be so savage that you're almost putting your competitors on call is like, until you get cheap and start like upping your game, I'm actually going to cheer for you. I mean, there's just so much going on in that statement, especially made in that year in 91, that it just some of this stuff is
turns.zh: 指数化的资产还只有今天的 0.2%，Vanguard 的市场份额也小得可怜。能有那种远见看到这一切上演，而且狂放到几乎是在给竞争对手“下战书”——“你们什么时候变便宜、什么时候提升水平，我反而会为你们欢呼”。那句话里的信息量太大了，尤其还是 91 年说的，有些东西真的

turns.en: mind blowing to me. But it's all kind of happened. And now we have a world where you can get Vanguardian funds anywhere easily. And that was the sort of that was his ultimate dream. And it's obviously now totally realized.
turns.zh: 让我目瞪口呆。但这些几乎都发生了。现在我们身处这样一个世界：你想买 Vanguard 式（Vanguardian）的基金，随处可得。那就是他最终的梦想，如今显然已经全部实现。

turns.en: Is there a downside to that, though, in the sense and try to follow me on this? Let's take fidelity. If they have a one basis point index fund, some people would say they're running a loss leader on that, I've realized they can do securities lending and those sorts of things. But if they're going to offer a one basis point index fund, maybe they're going to go chase down other product categories that are much more
turns.zh: 但这里面有没有反面？你跟上我的思路——就拿 Fidelity 来说。如果他们提供 1 个基点的指数基金，有人会说是亏本赚吆喝（loss leader）。我知道他们可以靠证券出借之类的名堂赚回来。但如果他们要提供 1 个基点的指数基金，也许就会去追逐那些贵得多的其他产品类别——

turns.en: expensive, that say Jack Bogle would frown upon investors holding those in a portfolio. So the easy one to point to, of course, is crypto or something like that, even though a lot of the crypto ETFs are pretty cheap. Is that the other side of that competition that in order for BlackRock and fidelity to compete with somebody like Vanguard, and that mutual ownership structure, they got to go after these more exotic
turns.zh: 那些 Jack Bogle 会皱眉、不希望投资者拿在组合里的那类。最容易点名的当然是加密之类——尽管很多加密 ETF 其实也不贵。这算不算竞争的另一面：BlackRock 和 Fidelity 为了与 Vanguard 及其共同所有制结构竞争，不得不去追逐这些更花哨、

turns.en: products that maybe aren't quite as good for investors. Yeah. And look, these firms, because in Fidelity's case, they have private shareholders and owners. And in BlackRock's case, they have actual shareholders, you know, like they're a publicly traded company. And BlackRock stock price has been really good compared to like, Franklin and T Rowe, because they've done a good job chasing down all these trends. BlackRock
turns.zh: 未必对投资者更好的产品？嗯，你看这些公司——Fidelity 背后是私人股东和所有人，BlackRock 是有真正股东的上市公司。BlackRock 的股价比 Franklin、T. Rowe 好太多了，就是因为他们把这些趋势追了个遍。BlackRock

turns.en: is probably the best example. They are into everything. They are into tech. They sell data, they have Aladdin, they have like, institutional clients, they do alternatives, they're in real estate. I mean, they are like, I always say they're like the equivalent of and they're the biggest asset manager. But they act like they're like young and scrappy. I always say my metaphor for BlackRock is they're like a 12 year NBA All-Star
turns.zh: 大概是最好的例子。他们什么都做：科技、卖数据、有 Aladdin，有机构客户、做另类投资、做房地产。我常说，他们虽然是最大的资产管理人，却活得像个年轻能拼的选手。我给 BlackRock 的比喻是：他们像一个 12 届 NBA 全明星，

turns.en: who still dives on the floor for lose balls. And that is what it takes to compete with Vanguard. You got to be big and totally scrappy hustle. Fidelity is, I think, fortunate that the market keeps going up. They're a good company, they've adapted, they've gone to index funds, they've had a lot of success there. They've actually done good in crypto, they have a brokerage, they have advisory business, they have a lot of
turns.zh: 还愿意鱼跃扑地板球。与 Vanguard 竞争需要的就是这个——既要大，又要彻底地能拼、死拼。Fidelity 我觉得幸运在市场一直涨。他们是家好公司，也在适应、做指数基金，而且做得很成功；加密方面其实也做得不错；还有经纪业务、顾问业务，很多线
